THE COVENANT PASSES TO YITZHAK — CHAPTERS 26 THROUGH 28

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 26 Yitzhak and Avimelekh

26:1 And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Avraham. And Yitzhak went to Avimelekh king of the Pelishtim, to Gerar.

26:2 And YHWH appeared to him, and said: Do not go down to Mitzrayim; dwell in the land which I shall tell you.

26:3 Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you; for to you, and to your descendants, I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Avraham your father.

26:4 And I will multiply your descendants as the stars of the heavens, and will give to your descendants all these lands; and by your descendants shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;

26:5 because Avraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

26:6 And Yitzhak dwelt in Gerar.

26:7 And the men of the place asked him about his wife; and he said: She is my sister; for he was afraid to say, My wife, lest, he thought, the men of the place should kill me for Rivkah, because she was fair to look upon.

26:8 And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Avimelekh king of the Pelishtim looked out at a window, and saw, and behold, Yitzhak was caressing Rivkah his wife.

26:9 And Avimelekh called Yitzhak, and said: Behold, surely she is your wife; and how did you say, She is my sister? And Yitzhak said to him: Because I said, Lest I die because of her.

26:10 And Avimelekh said: What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.

26:11 And Avimelekh charged all the people, saying: He who touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.

26:12 And Yitzhak sowed in that land, and found in the same year a hundredfold; and YHWH blessed him.

26:13 And the man grew great, and grew more and more until he became very great.

26:14 And he had possessions of flocks, and possessions of herds, and a great household; and the Pelishtim envied him.

26:15 Now all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Avraham his father, the Pelishtim had stopped, and filled with earth.

26:16 And Avimelekh said to Yitzhak: Go from us; for you are much mightier than we.

26:17 And Yitzhak departed from there, and encamped in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.

26:18 And Yitzhak dug again the wells of water, which they had dug in the days of Avraham his father, for the Pelishtim had stopped them after the death of Avraham; and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.

26:19 And Yitzhak's servants dug in the valley, and found there a well of living water.

26:20 And the herdsmen of Gerar strove with Yitzhak's herdsmen, saying: The water is ours. And he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.

26:21 And they dug another well, and they strove for that also. And he called the name of it Sitnah.

26:22 And he moved from there, and dug another well; and for that they did not strive. And he called the name of it Rechovot; and he said: For now YHWH has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.

26:23 And he went up from there to Be'er-Sheva.

26:24 And YHWH appeared to him the same night, and said: I am the Creator of Avraham your father. Fear not, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your descendants for my servant Avraham's sake.

26:25 And he built an altar there, and called upon the name of YHWH, and pitched his tent there; and there Yitzhak's servants dug a well.

26:26 Then Avimelekh went to him from Gerar, and Achuzat his friend, and Fikhol the captain of his host.

26:27 And Yitzhak said to them: Why have you come to me, seeing you hate me, and have sent me away from you?

26:28 And they said: We saw plainly that YHWH was with you; and we said, Let there be now an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,

26:29 that you will do us no harm, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace; you are now the blessed of YHWH.

26:30 And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.

26:31 And they rose up early in the morning, and swore one to another; and Yitzhak sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.

26:32 And it came to pass the same day, that Yitzhak's servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had dug, and said to him: We have found water.

26:33 And he called it Shivah; therefore the name of the city is Be'er-Sheva to this day.

26:34 And when Esav was forty years old, he took as wife Yehudit the daughter of Be'eri the Chiti, and Basemat the daughter of Eilon the Chiti.

26:35 And they were a source of bitterness of spirit to Yitzhak and to Rivkah.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session. Note on a real MT-internal tension, not a cross-witness variant, flagged forward: v.34 names Esav’s wives as Yehudit daughter of Be’eri the Chiti and Basemat daughter of Eilon the Chiti; ch.36:2-3 gives a different pairing (Adah daughter of Eilon the Chiti; Oholivamah daughter of Tzivon the Chivi; Basemat daughter of Yishma’el). A real, long-noted discrepancy within MT itself across these two chapters -- recorded here and flagged forward for ch.36, not resolved by harmonization at either location.

[CRITICAL NOTE] This chapter is a real, well-documented literary doublet of the wife-sister motif at ch.12 and ch.20, now recurring a third time -- noted as before, not adjudicated as evidence of composite authorship. Verse 5’s attribution to Avraham of having kept "my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws" (מצותי חקותי ותורתי) is a genuine, disclosed anachronism-adjacent crux: this is legislative terminology used elsewhere in the Torah for the Sinai revelation, applied here to a patriarch who lived generations before Sinai. Rendered literally; the crux is disclosed, not resolved by softening the terminology or reading it proleptically.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 27 The Stolen Blessing

27:1 And it came to pass, that when Yitzhak was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esav his elder son, and said to him: My son; and he said to him: Here I am.

27:2 And he said: Behold now, I am old, I do not know the day of my death.

27:3 Now therefore take, please, your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and hunt game for me;

27:4 and make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless you before I die.

27:5 And Rivkah heard when Yitzhak spoke to Esav his son. And Esav went to the field to hunt for game, and to bring it.

27:6 And Rivkah spoke to Ya'akov her son, saying: Behold, I heard your father speak to Esav your brother, saying:

27:7 Bring me game, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless you before YHWH before my death.

27:8 Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to what I command you.

27:9 Go now to the flock, and fetch me from there two good kids of the goats; and I will make them into savory food for your father, such as he loves.

27:10 And you shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, that he may bless you before his death.

27:11 And Ya'akov said to Rivkah his mother: Behold, Esav my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.

27:12 Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon myself, and not a blessing.

27:13 And his mother said to him: Upon me be your curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go, fetch them to me.

27:14 And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother; and his mother made savory food, such as his father loved.

27:15 And Rivkah took the finest garments of Esav her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Ya'akov her younger son;

27:16 and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck.

27:17 And she gave the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Ya'akov.

27:18 And he came to his father, and said: My father; and he said: Here I am; who are you, my son?

27:19 And Ya'akov said to his father: I am Esav your firstborn; I have done as you told me. Arise, please, sit and eat of my game, that your soul may bless me.

27:20 And Yitzhak said to his son: How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son? And he said: Because YHWH your Creator sent it to me.

27:21 And Yitzhak said to Ya'akov: Come near, please, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are truly my son Esav or not.

27:22 And Ya'akov went near to Yitzhak his father; and he felt him, and said: The voice is Ya'akov's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esav.

27:23 And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy, like his brother Esav's hands; so he blessed him.

27:24 And he said: Are you truly my son Esav? And he said: I am.

27:25 And he said: Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's game, that my soul may bless you. And he brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.

27:26 And his father Yitzhak said to him: Come near now, and kiss me, my son.

27:27 And he came near, and kissed him; and he smelled the smell of his garments, and blessed him, and said: See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which YHWH has blessed.

27:28 Therefore may the Creator give you of the dew of the heavens, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and wine.

27:29 Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you; be lord over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you; cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be he who blesses you.

27:30 And it came to pass, as soon as Yitzhak had finished blessing Ya'akov, and Ya'akov had scarcely gone out from the presence of Yitzhak his father, that Esav his brother came in from his hunting.

27:31 And he also made savory food, and brought it to his father, and said to his father: Let my father arise, and eat of his son's game, that your soul may bless me.

27:32 And Yitzhak his father said to him: Who are you? And he said: I am your son, your firstborn, Esav.

27:33 And Yitzhak trembled exceedingly, and said: Who then is he that hunted game, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of it all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, and he shall be blessed.

27:34 When Esav heard the words of his father, he cried out with a great and exceedingly bitter cry, and said to his father: Bless me, even me also, O my father.

27:35 And he said: Your brother came with deceit, and has taken away your blessing.

27:36 And he said: Is he not rightly named Ya'akov? For he has supplanted me these two times; he took away my birthright, and behold, now he has taken away my blessing. And he said: Have you not reserved a blessing for me?

27:37 And Yitzhak answered and said to Esav: Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants; and with grain and wine I have sustained him; and what then shall I do for you, my son?

27:38 And Esav said to his father: Do you have but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esav lifted up his voice, and wept.

27:39 And Yitzhak his father answered and said to him: Behold, your dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the heavens from above;

27:40 and by your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother; and it shall come to pass, when you become restless, that you shall break his yoke from off your neck.

27:41 And Esav hated Ya'akov because of the blessing with which his father blessed him; and Esav said in his heart: The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will slay my brother Ya'akov.

27:42 And these words of Esav her elder son were told to Rivkah; and she sent and called Ya'akov her younger son, and said to him: Behold, your brother Esav comforts himself concerning you, purposing to kill you.

27:43 Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; arise, flee to Lavan my brother, to Charan;

27:44 and stay with him a few days, until your brother's fury turns away;

27:45 until your brother's anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him; then I will send, and fetch you from there. Why should I be deprived of you both in one day?

27:46 And Rivkah said to Yitzhak: I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Chet; if Ya'akov takes a wife of the daughters of Chet, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 36's ויעקבני ("he has supplanted me") is a real, disclosed wordplay on יעקב (Ya'akov), already flagged at 25:26 -- the text itself makes the etymology explicit here through Esav's own words, unlike the earlier occurrence where it was implicit. Verses 29 and 37's גביר/אדון-type "lord" language describes Ya'akov's household position over Esav (a human hierarchy within the family blessing), not a divine title, and required no Divine Name Policy application. Verse 20's יהוה אלהיך ("YHWH your Creator") is Ya'akov's own invocation of the divine name while impersonating Esav -- rendered per standing policy without added commentary on the irony of a deceiver's oath.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 28 Ya'akov's Dream at Beit-El

28:1 And Yitzhak called Ya'akov, and blessed him, and charged him, and said to him: You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Kena'an.

28:2 Arise, go to Padan-Aram, to the house of Betu'el your mother's father; and take yourself a wife from there, of the daughters of Lavan your mother's brother.

28:3 And El Shaddai bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may become a company of peoples;

28:4 and give you the blessing of Avraham, to you, and to your descendants with you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings, which the Creator gave to Avraham.

28:5 And Yitzhak sent Ya'akov away; and he went to Padan-Aram, to Lavan, son of Betu'el the Arami, brother of Rivkah, Ya'akov's and Esav's mother.

28:6 When Esav saw that Yitzhak had blessed Ya'akov, and sent him away to Padan-Aram to take a wife from there; and that as he blessed him he charged him, saying, You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Kena'an;

28:7 and that Ya'akov had obeyed his father and his mother, and had gone to Padan-Aram;

28:8 and Esav saw that the daughters of Kena'an did not please Yitzhak his father;

28:9 then Esav went to Yishma'el, and took, besides the wives he had, Machalat the daughter of Yishma'el, Avraham's son, the sister of Nevayot, to be his wife.

28:10 And Ya'akov went out from Be'er-Sheva, and went toward Charan.

28:11 And he came to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set; and he took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.

28:12 And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens; and behold, the angels of the Creator were ascending and descending on it.

28:13 And behold, YHWH stood beside him, and said: I am YHWH, the Creator of Avraham your father, and the Creator of Yitzhak; the land on which you lie, to you I will give it, and to your descendants.

28:14 And your descendants shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south; and in you and in your descendants shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

28:15 And behold, I am with you, and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land; for I will not leave you, until I have done that which I have spoken to you of.

28:16 And Ya'akov awoke from his sleep, and he said: Surely YHWH is in this place, and I did not know it.

28:17 And he was afraid, and said: How full of awe is this place; this is none other than the house of the Creator, and this is the gate of heaven.

28:18 And Ya'akov rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it.

28:19 And he called the name of that place Beit-El; but the name of that city was Luz at first.

28:20 And Ya'akov vowed a vow, saying: If the Creator will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,

28:21 so that I come again to my father's house in peace, then YHWH shall be my Creator;

28:22 and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be the Creator's house; and of all that you shall give me, I will surely give the tenth to you.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 3's אל שדי continues the standing El-compound-title practice (rendered "El Shaddai," cf. 17:1). Verse 13's נצב עליו ("stood beside him"/"stood above it") contains a genuine, disclosed grammatical ambiguity: the preposition's antecedent could be Ya'akov himself or the ladder just described -- the majority reading ("beside him") is followed, the alternative disclosed rather than excluded. Verses 19 and 22 both use the phrase בית אלהים ("house of the Creator") -- v.19 as the place-name Beit-El itself, v.22 as Ya'akov's own vow restating the identical phrase -- a real, deliberate wordplay in the Hebrew's own structure, preserved by using the same English wording at both occurrences rather than varying the translation.

YAAKOV IN PADDAN-ARAM — CHAPTERS 29 THROUGH 31

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 29 Ya'akov, Le'ah, and Rachel

29:1 Then Ya'akov lifted up his feet, and went to the land of the children of the east.

29:2 And he looked, and behold, a well in the field, and behold, three flocks of sheep lying there by it — for out of that well they watered the flocks — and the stone upon the well's mouth was large.

29:3 And there all the flocks would gather; and they would roll the stone from the well's mouth, and water the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well's mouth, in its place.

29:4 And Ya'akov said to them: My brothers, where are you from? And they said: We are from Charan.

29:5 And he said to them: Do you know Lavan, son of Nachor? And they said: We know him.

29:6 And he said to them: Is it well with him? And they said: It is well; and behold, Rachel his daughter comes with the sheep.

29:7 And he said: Behold, it is still high day, not time for the cattle to be gathered together; water the sheep, and go and feed them.

29:8 And they said: We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered together, and they roll the stone from the well's mouth; then we water the sheep.

29:9 While he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep; for she tended them.

29:10 And it came to pass, when Ya'akov saw Rachel, the daughter of Lavan his mother's brother, and the sheep of Lavan his mother's brother, that Ya'akov went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Lavan his mother's brother.

29:11 And Ya'akov kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.

29:12 And Ya'akov told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rivkah's son; and she ran and told her father.

29:13 And it came to pass, when Lavan heard the news of Ya'akov his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Lavan all these things.

29:14 And Lavan said to him: Surely you are my bone and my flesh. And he stayed with him a month.

29:15 And Lavan said to Ya'akov: Because you are my brother, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?

29:16 Now Lavan had two daughters; the name of the elder was Le'ah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

29:17 And Le'ah's eyes were weak; but Rachel was of beautiful form, and fair to look upon.

29:18 And Ya'akov loved Rachel; and he said: I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.

29:19 And Lavan said: It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man; stay with me.

29:20 And Ya'akov served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.

29:21 And Ya'akov said to Lavan: Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.

29:22 And Lavan gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.

29:23 And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Le'ah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in to her.

29:24 And Lavan gave to his daughter Le'ah, Zilpah his maidservant, as her maidservant.

29:25 And it came to pass in the morning, that behold, it was Le'ah; and he said to Lavan: What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?

29:26 And Lavan said: It is not so done in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.

29:27 Fulfill the week of this one, and we will give you the other also, for the service which you shall serve with me yet seven other years.

29:28 And Ya'akov did so, and fulfilled her week; and he gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.

29:29 And Lavan gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maidservant, to be her maidservant.

29:30 And he went in also to Rachel, and he loved Rachel more than Le'ah, and served with him yet seven other years.

29:31 And YHWH saw that Le'ah was hated, and he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.

29:32 And Le'ah conceived, and bore a son, and called his name Re'uven; for she said: Because YHWH has looked upon my affliction; for now my husband will love me.

29:33 And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said: Because YHWH has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also. And she called his name Shim'on.

29:34 And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said: Now this time will my husband be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons. Therefore his name was called Levi.

29:35 And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said: This time I will praise YHWH. Therefore she called his name Yehudah; and she stopped bearing.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 32-35 contain four consecutive, real, disclosed etymological wordplays embedded in the Hebrew narrative itself: ראובן (Re'uven) linked to ראה, "he has seen/looked upon"; שמעון (Shim'on) linked to שמע, "he has heard"; לוי (Levi) linked to לוה, "to be joined/attached"; יהודה (Yehudah) linked to ידה/הודות, "to praise." None of these are reproduced in the English wording itself; each is disclosed here rather than forced into the translation. Verse 17's רכות (Le'ah's eyes, "weak" or "tender") carries a real, disclosed range of meaning -- "weak/delicate" versus "tender/soft" as a term of contrast with Rachel's beauty rather than a defect -- the majority reading ("weak") is followed without asserting it as the only possible sense.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 30 The Tribes Born — Ya'akov's Flocks

30:1 And when Rachel saw that she bore Ya'akov no children, Rachel envied her sister; and she said to Ya'akov: Give me children, or else I die.

30:2 And Ya'akov's anger was kindled against Rachel; and he said: Am I in the Creator's stead, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?

30:3 And she said: Behold my maidservant Bilhah; go in to her, that she may bear upon my knees, and I also may be built up through her.

30:4 And she gave him Bilhah her maidservant as wife; and Ya'akov went in to her.

30:5 And Bilhah conceived, and bore Ya'akov a son.

30:6 And Rachel said: The Creator has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son. Therefore she called his name Dan.

30:7 And Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again, and bore Ya'akov a second son.

30:8 And Rachel said: With mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and have prevailed. And she called his name Naftali.

30:9 When Le'ah saw that she had stopped bearing, she took Zilpah her maidservant, and gave her to Ya'akov as wife.

30:10 And Zilpah, Le'ah's maidservant, bore Ya'akov a son.

30:11 And Le'ah said: Fortune has come. And she called his name Gad.

30:12 And Zilpah, Le'ah's maidservant, bore Ya'akov a second son.

30:13 And Le'ah said: Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy. And she called his name Asher.

30:14 And Re'uven went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Le'ah. Then Rachel said to Le'ah: Give me, please, some of your son's mandrakes.

30:15 And she said to her: Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? And would you take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said: Therefore he shall lie with you tonight, for your son's mandrakes.

30:16 And Ya'akov came from the field in the evening, and Le'ah went out to meet him, and said: You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.

30:17 And the Creator listened to Le'ah, and she conceived, and bore Ya'akov a fifth son.

30:18 And Le'ah said: The Creator has given me my hire, because I gave my maidservant to my husband. And she called his name Yissakhar.

30:19 And Le'ah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Ya'akov.

30:20 And Le'ah said: The Creator has endowed me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons. And she called his name Zevulun.

30:21 And afterward she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.

30:22 And the Creator remembered Rachel, and the Creator listened to her, and opened her womb.

30:23 And she conceived, and bore a son, and said: The Creator has taken away my reproach.

30:24 And she called his name Yosef, saying: May YHWH add to me another son.

30:25 And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Yosef, that Ya'akov said to Lavan: Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.

30:26 Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know my service with which I have served you.

30:27 And Lavan said to him: If now I have found favor in your eyes — I have observed the signs, and YHWH has blessed me for your sake.

30:28 And he said: Name your wages, and I will give it.

30:29 And he said to him: You know how I have served you, and how your cattle have fared with me.

30:30 For it was little which you had before I came, and it has increased abundantly; and YHWH has blessed you wherever I turned. And now, when shall I provide for my own house also?

This is a real, substantial internal MT tension across three separate passages (26:34, 28:9, 36:2-3), not resolved by harmonization here -- recorded as the text presents it in each location, with the divergence disclosed rather than smoothed into a single genealogy. This is an MT-internal phenomenon, not a cross-witness variant; no DSS, SP, or LXX evidence bearing on it was located this session.

37:1 And Ya'akov dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Kena'an.

37:2 These are the generations of Ya'akov. Yosef, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers, being still a lad, with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives; and Yosef brought an evil report of them to their father.

37:3 Now Yisra'el loved Yosef more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age; and he made him a coat of many colors.

37:4 And when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him.

37:5 And Yosef dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers; and they hated him yet the more.

37:6 And he said to them: Hear, please, this dream which I have dreamed:

37:7 for behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves came around, and bowed down to my sheaf.

37:8 And his brothers said to him: Shall you indeed reign over us? Or shall you indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.

37:9 And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and said: Behold, I have dreamed yet a dream; and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.

37:10 And he told it to his father, and to his brothers; and his father rebuked him, and said to him: What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to you to the earth?

37:11 And his brothers envied him; but his father kept the matter in mind.

37:12 And his brothers went to feed their father's flock in Shekhem.

37:13 And Yisra'el said to Yosef: Do your brothers not feed the flock in Shekhem? Come, and I will send you to them. And he said to him: Here I am.

37:14 And he said to him: Go now, see whether it is well with your brothers, and well with the flock; and bring me back word. So he sent him from the valley of Chevron, and he came to Shekhem.

37:15 And a certain man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field; and the man asked him, saying: What are you seeking?

37:16 And he said: I am seeking my brothers. Tell me, please, where they are feeding the flock.

37:17 And the man said: They have departed from here; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dotan. And Yosef went after his brothers, and found them in Dotan.

37:18 And they saw him from afar, and before he came near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.

37:19 And they said to one another: Behold, this dreamer comes.

37:20 Come now therefore, and let us kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say, An evil beast has devoured him; and we shall see what will become of his dreams.

37:21 And Re'uven heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said: Let us not take his life.

37:22 And Re'uven said to them: Shed no blood; cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but lay no hand on him — that he might deliver him out of their hand, to restore him to his father.

37:23 And it came to pass, when Yosef came to his brothers, that they stripped Yosef of his coat, the coat of many colors that was on him;

37:24 and they took him, and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

37:25 And they sat down to eat bread; and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a caravan of Yishme'elim came from Gil'ad, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Mitzrayim.

37:26 And Yehudah said to his brothers: What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

37:27 Come, and let us sell him to the Yishme'elim, and let not our hand be on him; for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brothers listened to him.

37:28 And Midyanite traders passed by; and they drew and lifted Yosef up out of the pit, and sold Yosef to the Yishme'elim for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Yosef into Mitzrayim.

37:29 And Re'uven returned to the pit; and behold, Yosef was not in the pit; and he tore his clothes.

37:30 And he returned to his brothers, and said: The child is gone; and as for me, where shall I go?

37:31 And they took Yosef's coat, and killed a male goat, and dipped the coat in the blood;

37:32 and they sent the coat of many colors, and brought it to their father, and said: This we have found; know now whether it is your son's coat or not.

37:33 And he recognized it, and said: It is my son's coat; an evil beast has devoured him; Yosef is without doubt torn in pieces.

37:34 And Ya'akov tore his garments, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days.

37:35 And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said: No, but I will go down to the grave to my son, mourning. And his father wept for him.
